# Auth identity cleanup contract

The current catalog selects this extension of `convex-auth-437831bd-disposabl.7.tgz`. Product `users/authDeletion.ts` coordinates the four fences and bounded cleanup. The original vendor-only candidate did not change selection or orchestration; those were integrated separately. The bounded independent email-write and archive-parity reviews described below are complete; selection is not production deployment evidence. Archive SHA-256: `2a84ec66965d64507439ced99899b3fa227b6f79d8437305435cdd074849aa40`. Source patch SHA-256: `979b80c9a942ee450b725f9f306574635bc21166ae9c0393e5755ba69ca12422`. Applying the patch with `patch -p1` to the unpacked `.7` package reproduces its `.8` source. The package includes source, compiled runtime, public and internal declarations; rebuild with the same upstream build instructions in `README.md`, setting version `.8`.

The username component exposes app-server-only `public.eraseUser({ userId })`: atomically insert a permanent user-ID tombstone and delete the username. `setUsername` rejects that ID after the tombstone commits. The email component exposes app-server-only `verifiedEmails.eraseUserBatch({ userId })`: atomically establish its permanent fence and delete up to 100 verified-email rows and 100 attributed challenge rows. Continue until `complete` is true; a full 100-row batch intentionally needs another call. The existing unfenced `deleteUsername` and unbounded `deleteUser` are retained for compatibility and must not be treated as these erasure operations. New attributed email challenges reject erased IDs and claims of existing attributed challenges fail after the fence. The tombstones retain opaque user IDs and timestamps indefinitely; neither anonymous data nor a retention policy is established.

Integration must establish core/password/username/email fences in one app-server mutation before core mappings can be purged or deletion can be reported complete. Continue the bounded email and existing core/password batches until all report complete; perform independent authorization, retry and orchestration review. The email API purges only rows indexed by `purpose.userId`. Custom challenges started without an attributed user ID are not safely associable here, may remain until existing expiry cleanup, and cannot be counted as erased. The patch does not address other components, old unattributed rows, provider identities, retention policy, or whole-account deletion. Re-registration under the same old user ID is denied; no tombstone removal policy is supplied.

Fixture code is product-only. The reset inventories exclude `packages/tests/fixtures/auth-identity-erasure-convex`; preserve that exclusion and its packaging proof. Frozen-install, generator, product integration, and source/compiled local fixture results are recorded in the delivery handoff. They do not replace independent archive review or establish production deployment and complete erasure.

The independent 2026-11-09 email-write review enumerated the three production verified-email insertion paths, `addEmail`, `changeEmail`, and `signUp`, and traced their attributed challenge creation and claim checks in source and compiled JavaScript. It found no tombstone bypass in that scope. Custom challenge completion does not insert verified emails; recovery rechecks the current verified owner. Legacy `deleteUser` remains unfenced and must not replace `eraseUserBatch`. This was static inspection, not a fixture rerun. A separate static review completed the `.7`-to-`.8` archive delta, username operations, validators and declaration parity. The inventories match with no added or removed files and 44 changed files. Applying the patch reproduced the full `.8` source tree byte-for-byte; unchanged core and Google files were preserved. Username set and erase use the same indexed tombstone within their mutations, and the new operation signatures agree across runtime validators and declaration outputs. Neither review reran the fixtures or establishes provider behavior, retention approval or whole-account deletion.
